correctness.rationale: For arbitrary a,b,g>0 the direct sinc/cos intensity expansion yields c2=-s^4/12-r(d^2-s^2/4) and c4=s^6/360+qs^2/12+q^2/(12r)-qr/12, s=a+b, r=ab, d=g+s/2, q=rg(g+s)>0. The equation qr^2+yr-q^2=0 has exactly one positive root; the quadratic length roots and positive gap recover the geometry up to reflection. Monotonicity in r proves the sharp feasible-jet bound and continuous ambiguity at order two. Independent exact-rational double-moment integration and direct Fourier tests in CHECK.py passed 1315 checks. Limits: no noisy-derivative stability, no more than two intervals.

value.rationale: A recent two-interval theorem required complete continuous Fourier magnitudes. Exact recovery from only three natural local Taylor measurements is a meaningful information-minimal inverse theorem, with a radical reconstruction, an impossibility result for all lower-order even Taylor data, and a sharp semialgebraic feasible-data boundary detecting equal-length intervals. This is neither a table recomputation nor a simple restatement of full-data uniqueness; it may serve exact inverse-problem design, although practical noisy derivative estimation is outside scope.
